name: windows-baseline
title: Windows endpoint & server baseline
description: High-value Windows hardening checks: Defender, firewall, BitLocker, UAC, legacy protocols, RDP, accounts and updates. Read-only registry and PowerShell reads; inspired by the Microsoft Security Baselines and CIS Windows Benchmarks, not certified content.

rules.title: Defender real-time protection is on
rules.rationale: Real-time protection is the control that stops known malware at execution time.

rules.title: Windows Firewall is on for every profile
rules.rationale: A disabled profile exposes every listening service on networks of that type.

rules.title: BitLocker protects the system drive
rules.rationale: Without disk encryption, physical access to the device is access to its data and cached credentials.

rules.title: User Account Control is enabled
rules.rationale: UAC separates administrative actions from the everyday session; disabling it makes every process an admin process.

rules.title: SMBv1 server protocol is disabled
rules.rationale: SMBv1 is the protocol behind EternalBlue/WannaCry and has no supported use.

rules.title: Remote Desktop requires Network Level Authentication
rules.rationale: Without NLA an unauthenticated client reaches the full logon stack — the surface BlueKeep-class bugs live in.

rules.title: Guest account is disabled
rules.rationale: An enabled Guest account is an unauthenticated foothold.

rules.title: automatic updates are not disabled by policy
rules.rationale: Patches that wait for a human do not happen.

rules.title: LSA protection (RunAsPPL) is enabled
rules.rationale: LSA protection blocks credential-dumping tools from reading LSASS memory.
